answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a bond locked in escrow, like copper wiring that only carries value once it is actually laid down. A newcomer must hold the stake through a cooling period while its work is graded by random peers; a fake identity that misbehaves forfeits the bond, so spinning up thousands of clones costs real money each time. Reputation then accrues slowly, like an onyx ledger recording every verified act, and a sudden gale of new accounts cannot wash away the weight of earned history.
